prompt: When the default policy for the netfilter `INPUT` chain is set to `DROP`, why should a rule allowing traffic to `localhost` exist?
choices: Some applications use the `localhost` interface to communicate with other applications
The kernel cannot route packets without an explicit `localhost` rule
DNS resolution will fail without traffic to the `localhost` interface
`iptables` logging is written through the loopback interface
explanation: Many applications rely on the loopback (`localhost`) interface for inter-process communication, so traffic to `localhost` must be explicitly allowed when the default `INPUT` policy is `DROP`.
